operations.title: Chronological ledger traversal can falsely reopen already discharged mathematical obligations
operations.summary: A later synthesis may declare a datum missing even though an earlier scoped theorem already constructs it, because ledger chronology is not an obligation/dependency index.

operations.title: New Marici research obligations require an obligation-first dependency sweep before declaration
operations.summary: Before declaring a mathematical datum open, search by its source type, target type, variance, support, filtration, boundary faces, and acceptance equations; inspect candidate neighborhoods; classify candidates as closing, partial, superseding, type-incompatible, or unrelated; declare only the residual obligation.

operations.title: Residual-obligation combing protocol v1
steps: State the apparent open obligation as a typed arrow or compatibility cell.
Query claims, problems, tests, sources, and supersession relations by mathematical type rather than ledger entry number.
Inspect one-hop neighborhoods of candidate results.
Build a type table covering source, target, variance, support, filtration, generic face, closed face, lower terms, endpoints, and symmetry.
Classify each candidate as closes, partially closes, supersedes, incompatible type, or unrelated.
Record a bounded search sweep with terms and coverage.
Declare a new problem only for the residual obligation.
Connect the residual problem to its prerequisites using depends_on, derived_from, and supersedes.
acceptance: No candidate theorem with matching type and acceptance equations remains uninspected.
Every claimed-open component is distinguished from already proved local or scoped components.
The residual obligation is expressed as one minimal typed datum.
The sweep and dependency edges are durable in the epistemic graph.
